stem: A client taking digoxin is newly prescribed verapamil. Which interaction should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Verapamil lowers serum digoxin concentrations during the first week, so the digoxin dose usually needs to be increased to preserve therapeutic effect.
options.B: Verapamil can raise serum digoxin concentrations substantially during the first week, so digoxin levels and toxicity should be monitored and dose reduction considered.
options.C: Verapamil changes digoxin absorption but not serum concentration, so routine monitoring for digoxin toxicity is unnecessary when the drugs are combined.
options.D: Verapamil prevents digitalis toxicity by increasing digoxin clearance, so the combination permits higher digoxin doses without extra monitoring for toxicity or drug levels.

rationale: Current VERELAN PM labeling states that chronic verapamil treatment can increase serum digoxin concentrations by 50% to 75% during the first week of therapy and that this can result in digitalis toxicity. The label directs clinicians to consider reducing the digoxin dose and to monitor digoxin levels periodically. Therefore B is correct. A, C and D reverse or deny the documented interaction.
educational_objective: Recognize that verapamil can increase digoxin exposure and toxicity risk; monitor digoxin levels and clinical toxicity and consider dose reduction when the drugs are combined.

source_original.stem: A client taking digoxin is newly prescribed verapamil. Which interaction should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Verapamil lowers serum digoxin concentrations during the first week, so the digoxin dose usually needs to be increased to preserve therapeutic effect.
options.B: Verapamil can raise serum digoxin concentrations substantially during the first week, so digoxin levels and toxicity should be monitored and dose reduction considered.
options.C: Verapamil changes digoxin absorption but not serum concentration, so routine monitoring for digoxin toxicity is unnecessary when the drugs are combined.
options.D: Verapamil prevents digitalis toxicity by increasing digoxin clearance, so the combination permits higher digoxin doses without extra monitoring for toxicity or drug levels.

source_original.rationale: Verapamil labeling reports that chronic verapamil treatment can increase serum digoxin concentrations by about 50–75% during the first week and recommends monitoring and dose reduction as needed to avoid digitalis toxicity. Option B reflects that interaction. Option A reverses the effect. Option C incorrectly says serum concentration is unaffected. Option D incorrectly claims increased clearance and lower toxicity risk.
source_original.source_detail: DailyMed VERELAN PM (verapamil hydrochloride) — Drug Interactions, §7.4 Digitalis: chronic verapamil can increase serum digoxin concentrations about 50–75% during the first week; monitor and reduce digoxin dose as needed to avoid toxicity. Current FDA VERELAN PM labeling at the cited DailyMed set ID; live version rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, calculations, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Corrected the exact DailyMed locator from §7.4 to current §7.5 Digitalis. Retained the directly label-supported 50–75% first-week interaction and monitoring/dose-reduction principle.

audit_findings.claim_audit: 50–75%, first-week timing, toxicity risk, periodic level monitoring and dose reduction consideration are directly label-supported.

distractor_audit.C: Incorrectly denies serum-concentration change and monitoring need.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B is compatible with the label.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices concern the same interaction construct.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second pass caught and corrected the locator numbering; no unresolved precision remains.
